title: Plan in weeks. Report in months. From one model.
summary: Plan in weeks. Report in months. From one model.
body_markdown:
**Short version:** Abacum now supports weekly-timescale financial models that roll up automatically to monthly, quarterly, and yearly reporting, from one connected model.


The month is an accounting convention. It is not how most businesses actually operate.


Collections land on a weekly cycle. Media and events spend commits weekly. Retail, hospitality and CPG run 4-4-5 calendars where a fiscal month is a bundle of weeks, not a page on a wall calendar. Revenue operations teams pace weekly, report weekly, and hold their pipeline meeting on a Monday. Finance is the one function in the building still translating all of it into months, because that is the only rhythm the planning software understands.


The translation has a cost, and every finance team pays it in the same place: the weekly file that lives outside the platform.


## The spreadsheet that never leaves


Ask a finance team which model they rebuild by hand most often and the answer is usually the 13-week direct cash flow forecast. It is the most requested artefact in finance and one of the few that a CFO reads line by line, because liquidity is a weekly question. A monthly cash view tells you that you ended the quarter fine. It does not tell you which Thursday you were tight.


So the 13-week sits in a spreadsheet. Someone rebuilds it every Monday from exports, pastes in the week's collections and payments, and reconciles it against the monthly plan that lives in the planning platform. Two systems, two versions of the truth, one person holding them together.


This is the part worth being precise about, because it is where most tools stop short. The problem is not that finance teams lack a weekly view. Plenty of tools can display weeks. The problem is that weekly planning and monthly planning live in separate places and get reconciled by hand. Adding a weekly module beside the monthly one does not fix that. It formalizes it.


A finance team does not want to plan weekly instead of monthly. They want to plan weekly and report monthly, from the same numbers, without anyone doing the arithmetic between them.


## Weekly Planning & Reporting, now in Abacum


You can now build models at weekly timescale in Abacum, with weekly formulas and weekly actuals flowing in from your connected data. Those weeks roll up to months, quarters and years automatically, with no mapping layer to maintain and no reconciliation step.


Three things change in practice:


-


**Build at weekly timescale.** Choose weekly when you create the model. Formulas then operate at week level, so .t-1 means last week. Weekly actuals flow in against weekly plan, and variance is a weekly number rather than a monthly average you have to interpret.


-


**Report in weeks, and in months, from the same model.** Tables, charts and KPI cards all read weekly, with a calendar view and week-based presets. The same variable reports by week to your operations team and by month to your board, out of one model.


-


**Feed monthly models from weekly ones.** A monthly model reads weekly variables directly, aggregating them the way each variable should aggregate, whether that is a sum, an average, or the first or last value in the period. Your weekly cash detail and your monthly board pack come from the same source, and nobody keeps them in step by hand.


## The 13-week cash flow, on live data


The clearest test of this is the model everyone maintains manually. Build a weekly model, connect your collections and payments data, and the 13-week direct cash flow forecast runs inside the platform on real numbers.


The weekly rebuild stops. Enter and edit weekly assumptions in a pivoted Input Table and watch them recalculate against actuals as the week closes. When the CFO asks what changed since last week, the answer takes a click rather than a morning.


The same shape applies well beyond cash. Weekly media and campaign spend against committed budget. Weekly subscription and retention pacing. Weekly store or venue performance on a 4-4-5 calendar that finally matches the fiscal calendar the business actually closes on.


## One model, both cadences


Weekly planning is not new to the category, and we will not pretend otherwise. What is worth your attention is where the weekly sits.


In Abacum, weekly is not a module bolted beside monthly. The same Engine runs both. Weekly variables feed monthly models with proper time aggregation, and the organization's weekly calendar, which defines the week start day, the month roll-up rule, and where week one begins, maps every transaction date to both a week and a fiscal month. A majority-rule calendar and a fixed 4-4-5, 4-5-4 or 5-4-4 calendar are both first-class.


That is the difference that matters day to day. Weekly detail and monthly reporting stop being two jobs. Finance runs one connected model and chooses the lens.


## Who feels it first


-


**FP&A teams:** the weekly file comes back inside the platform. The Monday rebuild disappears and the time goes into reading the forecast instead of assembling it.


-


**CFOs and VPs of Finance:** weekly cash visibility stops being a reporting preference and becomes what it actually is, a liquidity control. Businesses with tight working capital cycles get a view they can act on inside the week, not a month later.


-


**Operations and revenue teams:** finance finally meets them on the cadence they already run. No translation, no lag, no separate version of the number.


## Plan on your rhythm, not the calendar's


Finance teams have spent years bending a weekly business into monthly buckets because the software asked them to. The bending was never the job.


Plan in weeks. Report in months. Run both from one model on live data.
